about: Client cache of mod.io mod-list query results, ls::ugc::ModListCachedRequestSystem: HashMap<ls::ugc::ModItemListInfoID, ls::ugc::ModItemListInfoResponse> (macOS ~HashMap of that type) plus a DynamicArray<ModItemListInfoID> at +0x40 (pending queries, as in the sibling CacheModDependencies/CacheModInfo singletons). The map is written out member by member because its key is a struct. Response (0x18 bytes): Array of 0x140-byte mod entries + 8 bytes; the entry holds six STDStrings (+0x00..+0x78), Arrays at +0x98 (0x50-byte elements), +0xA8 and +0xB8 (STDString), +0xC8 (0x30-byte elements) and a HashSet at +0xD8 (dtor bg3.exe+0x38B5D20). Live: idle, all zero.

evidence.says: bucket array of the HashMap; creator bg3.exe+0x3BEF1F0 allocates 0x50 and zeroes it (HashMap pattern + Array at +0x40); destructor bg3.exe+0x3B7A730 ends with HashSet<ModItemListInfoID> dtor bg3.exe+0x11FC4C0 on +0
keys ModItemListInfoID (0x38); macOS ls::HashMap<ModItemListInfoID, ModItemListInfoResponse>::~HashMap; Windows key count at +0x2C drives the value loop in bg3.exe+0x3B7D7D0

ModItemListInfoResponse per key, stride 0x18: bg3.exe+0x3B7D7D0 clears the Array at value+0 (bg3.exe+0x38BB8A0, element stride 0x140, element dtor bg3.exe+0x38B5D20) and frees it, then the dtor frees *(this+0x30)
size of the uninitialised value storage

Windows dtor bg3.exe+0x3B7A730 resizes +0x40 to 0 with bg3.exe+0x11FC8C0 (stride 0x38, moves exactly the ModItemListInfoID members) and frees it; macOS has DynamicArray<ls::ugc::ModItemListInfoID>; 'pending' role by analogy with the sibling cache singletons Role confirmed on Windows: bg3.exe+0x3BEE060 keeps the 0x38-stride array at +0x40 (count +0x4C) as an LRU list - 'while (10 < count)' it pops the last query, destroys it (bg3.exe+0x11FCB50) and removes its response from the map (key compare bg3.exe+0x15F83E0 over the 0x38-stride keys at +0x20) - capping the cache at 10 query results.

survey.live_reason: only empty (all-zero) instances were seen: the member boundaries are untested
open_questions: Member names of ModItemListInfoID (tags, counts, search text are guesses not written into names); layout of the 0x140-byte mod entry and of the 8 bytes after the response array (kept inside the raw value storage).
survey.second_pass: Container positions, the 0x38-byte query key (Windows destructor bg3.exe+0x11FCB50 and mover bg3.exe+0x11FC8C0) and the 0x18-byte response stride were already from Windows code; the role of the +0x40 array is now settled from bg3.exe+0x3BEE060 as an LRU list capped at 10 entries.
